reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) concerns the corrosion behavior of high-entropy alloy coatings on Q235 steel, not the effect of mechanical polishing on the bare Q235 substrate's surface heterogeneities. No evidence is provided to support the key premises about polishing removing defects, forming a protective oxide, or the temperature dependence.
premises: Surface heterogeneities (inclusions, oxide discontinuities) on Q235 steel act as preferential sites for localized anodic reactions in chloride environments.
Mechanical polishing can remove or reduce these surface heterogeneities.
A more uniform surface leads to a more protective oxide layer.
A more protective oxide layer retards pitting and localized corrosion initiation.
This effect holds at both room and elevated temperatures.
